findings.title: Four new NGIAB_* environment variables introduced by this commit are not documented in README.md
findings.detail: This commit adds NGIAB_UPLOAD_CONCURRENCY (ingest.py:50), NGIAB_JOB_STALE_SECONDS (ingest.py:59), NGIAB_LISTING_CONCURRENCY (run_store.py:62), and NGIAB_MAX_CONCURRENT_INGESTS (controllers.py:459). `git diff fa6674c -- README.md` is empty -- none of the four appear anywhere in README.md. README.md documents every other operator-tunable env var that shapes runtime behavior in a 'Hosted deployments' / 'Upgrading from an earlier version' section (NGIAB_STORAGE_BACKEND at line 99, NGIAB_SCAN_ROOTS at line 89, plus PORTAL_SUPERUSER_NAME/PASSWORD and TETHYS_SECRET_KEY). These four are exactly the kind of operator-facing tuning knob (concurrency ceilings, staleness timeout) that pattern covers, and an operator running a hosted deployment has no way to discover them without reading source.
findings.rule_basis: No single explicit sentence in README.md says 'every env var must be documented here', but the file's own established and consistent pattern is to document operator-configurable environment variables under 'Hosted deployments' / 'Upgrading from an earlier version'. This is an inferred convention rather than a literal quoted rule, hence moderate rather than high confidence.

findings.title: Pre-existing NGIAB_* env vars (from before this commit) are also undocumented in README.md
findings.detail: NGIAB_S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT (controllers.py:347, present at base commit fa6674c already) and NGIAB_LISTING_TTL_SECONDS (run_store.py:60, present at base commit already) are not mentioned in README.md. These predate this commit and are called out separately per the audit instructions -- not something introduced by this diff.

ci_gate_check.result: No CI escape found. pyproject.toml sets testpaths = ["tests"] with no --ignore/norecursedirs exclusions. The Dockerfile's `test` stage does `COPY . /build` (whole repo) before running `pytest -p no:cacheprovider --no-cov`, so both new files are picked up by normal pytest discovery inside the Docker test image the CI `pytest` job builds and runs. The 'prove it actually ran' executed-count guard in tests.yml will count these new tests toward `executed`, and neither file skips unconditionally, so they don't create a false-green via all-skipped.

comment_style_check.command: python3 scripts/check-comment-style.py (scans hardcoded ROOT = tethysapp/ngiab, plus public/frontend/*.js)
comment_style_check.result: checked comment style: 0 problem(s). No consecutive-comment-line violations in controllers.py, ingest.py, run_store.py, duckdb_conn.py, utils.py, or ngiab-upload-run.js. The new multi-paragraph docstrings in ingest.py/_workspace, _upload_directory, run_store.py/_delete_prefix/_is_missing, duckdb_conn.py/_with_fresh_credentials are all module/function-level docstrings, which the script explicitly exempts ('Docstrings are documentation and may be any length').

test_file_convention_check.result: Both new test files match existing conventions: module docstring in the same voice explaining *why* the file exists (compare tests/test_upload_hardening.py, tests/test_run_store.py), a locally-defined `storage_root` fixture identical in shape to the one already duplicated in tests/test_upload.py (not shared via conftest.py, consistent with existing per-file duplication pattern), `permitted`/`user` fixtures matching tests/test_upload.py exactly, and `# ---- section ----` comment banners matching the style used elsewhere in the suite (e.g. tests/test_backfill.py).

frontend_readme_check.layout_table_accuracy: The Layout table in public/frontend/README.md does not list components/ngiab-upload-run.js at all. This gap predates the commit under audit -- ngiab-upload-run.js was added in commit 4de4d5c and extended in 3e8bdb5, both before base fa6674c -- so it is pre_existing and not attributable to this diff. Not filed as a primary finding per the pre-existing-code rule.
frontend_readme_check.js_change_review: The two additions (POLL_CEILING_MS module-level comment, disconnectedCallback with a one-line comment) both respect the 'inside a function body, a comment is one line' convention and the doc-comment-may-be-any-length rule for the module-level ceiling comment. No markdown-link vs backtick vs @-inclusion concern applies (that convention governs SKILL.md/AGENTS.md reference files, not this repo's plain JS README, which uses prose links like `[filename.md](...)` and code-span references informally without a stated backtick/@ rule).

formatting_check.note: pyproject.toml declares yapf (facebook style, 120 columns) but no .flake8 file exists in the repo root, and .github/workflows/tests.yml has no yapf/flake8 CI job at all -- only comment-style.py, check-theme-tokens.py and check-contrast.py run in the 'comment-style' CI job, plus compileall/pyflakes/import-removal greps in 'backend'. Running yapf locally against the changed files surfaces many reformatting diffs, but they are pervasive across pre-existing, unchanged lines in the same files (e.g. blank-line-before-decorator conventions already violated at HEAD~ in controllers.py), indicating the codebase was never brought under yapf compliance to begin with. No line in the diff's added/changed content exceeds 120 columns. Given the lack of CI enforcement and pervasive pre-existing non-compliance, this is not filed as a commit-specific finding (would require judgment-free codebase-wide reformatting outside this commit's scope).

residual_risks: yapf/flake8 formatting standards declared in pyproject.toml have no CI gate and the codebase is not currently yapf-clean; this commit neither improves nor worsens that meaningfully, but a future 'make format-check pass' effort will touch these same files.

The Layout table in public/frontend/README.md is missing an entry for ngiab-upload-run.js (pre-existing, not introduced here); worth closing whenever that file is next touched for something other than a hotfix.
testing_gaps: components/ngiab-upload-run.js gained two new behaviors (a POLL_CEILING_MS backstop that reports a hung poll after an hour, and a disconnectedCallback guard that stops the poll loop when the element is removed) with no corresponding change to ngiab-upload-run.test.js (git diff shows zero changes to that file). The frontend README's own architecture section treats 'must unsubscribe in disconnectedCallback, or every mount leaks a listener' as a load-bearing contract worth testing elsewhere in the suite (e.g. layers.test.js covers the install-after-wipe contract by assertion, not screenshot), so the absence of a test asserting the poll loop actually stops after disconnect is a gap relative to that pattern, though not a violation of an explicit rule.
